fields.sample_size: 396 respondents in Koja, North Jakarta (surveyed residents, business owners and community-organisation members; cluster table totals 396: 296 in the adequate-health-standards cluster and 100 in the public-health-risk cluster), plus semi-structured interviews with local leaders, public health officials and NGO representatives (number not stated) and field observation; sampling procedure not described beyond "representative sample"
fields.effect_measure: exploratory factor analysis (three factors, 55.9% of variance), cluster analysis with chi-square tests, and a binary logistic regression of willingness to participate in community-based sanitation programmes (Table 4; Nagelkerke R2 0.129, overall classification 85.6%)
fields.effect_estimate: Logistic regression (Table 4): sanitation infrastructure and collaboration factor B = 0.408 (significant, positive); sanitation governance factor B = 0.087, Exp(B) 1.091, p = 0.530 and operational practices factor B = 0.103, Exp(B) 1.108, p = 0.468 (not significant); female B = -0.776 (p = 0.015, lower participation than men); at least a bachelor's degree B = 1.229 (p = 0.026); age under 29 B = -0.424 (p = 0.158); formal occupation B = -0.328 (p = 0.502); income above 5 million B = 0.106 (p = 0.835). Cluster comparison: income differs between the clusters (chi2 = 9.632, p = 0.022) while gender, age and education do not. The authors conclude that infrastructure and collaboration, gender and education shape participation and call for integrated, inclusive sanitation policies; governance quality as measured by monitoring and aesthetics did not predict participation.
fields.section: Full text (14 pages): Method; Results and Discussion (Tables 1-4: EFA, clusters, chi-square, logistic model); Conclusion
fields.exact_location: Table 1 (EFA), Table 3 (cluster chi-square), Table 4 (logistic model); Conclusion; KEMAS 20(3):619-632

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a mixed-methods study of willingness to participate in community-based sanitation programmes in Koja, Jakarta (396 respondents; EFA, clusters, logistic regression); read in full text 2026-10-04. The exposure is perceived governance and infrastructure, not a legal or administrative rule.
pdf_note: Jurnal Kesehatan Masyarakat (KEMAS) 20(3):619-632, English, 14 pages read in full (Drive file S363_Sofiyah_2025...pdf); interview component not reported in detail
notes: The regression outcome is willingness to participate, not access; the study may be a candidate for an outcome-fit check (criterion 4).
